issue: Bash background PID publication did not establish that nohup had installed SIGHUP-ignore before terminal close.

runtime_review.ownership: signal_owned targets the live owned launcher/shell process group and the kernel-reported foreground group. It does not enumerate or terminate the whole terminal session. Maintenance closes the PTY and reaps already-exited children; it does not kill background nohup groups.
runtime_review.child_signal_setup: Terminal child launcher resets SIGHUP to default before exec, so inherited SIG_IGN in the workload establishes actual nohup behavior.

result.fixture: Real Bash PTY background child held at an explicit before-exec FIFO barrier; this exposes the PID-publication contract without a timing sleep.
result.conclusion: Bash $! readiness admits a live child before nohup has installed SIGHUP-ignore; this is a readiness-fixture defect, not a claim that an established nohup workload was killed.

old_predicate_reproduction.limits: Explicit FIFO barrier deterministically exposes pre-exec readiness; this is not a claim to have observed the original hosted process scheduling.

fixture_change.readiness: Actual nohup launches a Python workload. The workload asserts signal.getsignal(SIGHUP)==SIG_IGN, then publishes os.getpid(). No test code installs the ignored disposition itself.
preserved_assertions: owned child still exists after the original post-close poll interval
finally kills only the fixture-owned published PID; service context performs owned cleanup
